title: The Posture Review: Herceg-Bosna Between Conquest and Coalition
sources: ICTY Prlić et al. Trial Judgment (IT-04-74-T), territorial-control findings
ICTY Kordić & Čerkez Trial Judgment (IT-95-14/2-T), central Bosnia findings
content:
The Bosnian Croat war effort of 1993 was caught between two incompatible strategies, and the posture review forced a choice between them. One path — the maximalist project documented in the ICTY Prlić et al. Trial Judgment (IT-04-74-T) — pursued territorial control over the areas the Vance-Owen map had designated Croat-majority, including the central Bosnian municipalities where the ICTY Kordić & Čerkez Trial Judgment (IT-95-14/2-T) found a campaign of persecution against the Bosniak population. The other path pointed back toward coalition with the Sarajevo government against the common Serb adversary.

Pressing Croat territorial objectives meant doubling down on the war against the ARBiH in the Lašva Valley and Herzegovina — a war that consumed HVO strength, blackened Herceg-Bosna’s international standing, and opened a second front that benefited only the Bosnian Serbs. Coordinating with the Bosniaks meant subordinating the maximalist map to a partnership of necessity, trading the dream of a consolidated Croat space for the security of a shared front. Consolidating supply, or suing for the Federation framework, were way-stations between these poles — buying time or accepting the eventual logic of coalition.

The strategic incoherence was structural. The Herceg-Bosna project drew its arms and direction from Zagreb, but Zagreb’s own interests increasingly pointed toward the American-brokered partnership with Sarajevo that would crystallize in the 1994 Washington Agreement. A local leadership pressing for maximalist conquest was, in effect, fighting a war its patron was preparing to abandon.

The posture review thus posed the project’s defining contradiction in operational form. To press Croat objectives was to pursue the territory at the cost of the alliance — and ultimately at the cost of the patron’s patience. To accept the Federation framework was to surrender the maximalist ambition for a coalition that could actually be sustained. The historical record bent, after a year of ruinous fighting, toward the second.
